01 · Executive verdict · corrected 16 July mandate

One Australian web MVP. One fail-closed release authority. Native apps later.

GreyhoundIQ’s selected production shape is a Google defensive edge feeding Sydney and Melbourne Cloud Run cells, a contract-driven API boundary, a stateless modular monolith plus isolated workers, Australian object/event storage, and a single-writer PostgreSQL/Prisma data plane with rehearsed Melbourne recovery. Application realtime uses regional Cloud Run WebSocket gateways, an AlloyDB transactional outbox, AU-restricted Pub/Sub, separate per-region application Memorystore and cursor replay. Existing one-to-one voice/video uses independent self-hosted Sydney and Melbourne LiveKit cells with room-home assignment, per-cell HA Redis, tested N+1 SFU capacity, TLS signalling and explicit UDP/ICE/TURN paths; active calls do not migrate across a regional failure. There is no production user/customer dataset to migrate: AlloyDB is bootstrapped empty with forward-only Prisma migrations, synthetic staging fixtures and approved racing-provider rehydration. Native iOS/iPadOS and Android store apps remain separate post-MVP codebases and do not block web launch. Design Lab is the authenticated simulation, training, observability and Founder control layer—not a shortcut around protected production approval.

Top five risks

  1. The new target project has no verified architecture resources; every provider and deployment gate is still open.
  2. The legacy single-region workflow, Supabase deployment path and green-staging Terraform conflict with the selected target and must not be run.
  3. Cloud Storage, application realtime and the independent Sydney/Melbourne LiveKit/Redis/TURN cells remain unimplemented MVP blockers.
  4. Database normalisation, RLS authority and connection/transaction capacity have unresolved launch blockers.
  5. Racing feed lineage, Founder/staff controls, observability and compound recovery exercises remain unproven.

Top five immediate actions

  1. Finish the source-only production foundation and free-trial project preflight; do not create billable resources until separately approved.
  2. Freeze every data feed contract, lineage, cadence, freshness threshold, licence, owner and recovery runbook.
  3. Bootstrap empty AlloyDB with forward-only Prisma migrations, synthetic fixtures and approved provider rehydration; prove normalisation, pooling, restore and recovery.
  4. Complete Cloud Storage, the regional WebSocket/outbox/Pub/Sub/application-Redis path and independent regional LiveKit cells; then prove scoped Staff/Founder controls and the unified observability desk.
  5. Benchmark 1×/3×/10×, restore, fenced regional recovery and protected web promotion end to end; native store delivery remains post-MVP.

02
Facts · assumptions · missing inputs

Honest inputs before capacity

Repository evidence, the new-account read-only preflight and target design are labelled separately. Provisional workload values remain launch blockers until measured or approved.

Most important missing inputs: what “50,000 users” means; route mix and session length; real concurrency; CPU and memory per route; transaction duration and DB limits; response/upload sizes; cacheability; realtime connections/messages; feed/provider SLAs; data volume/growth/retention; legal residency; availability/RTO/RPO; cost ceiling; and trained on-call coverage.

Known code and new-account facts

  • Next.js/TypeScript web application; native iOS/iPadOS and Android store apps are separate post-MVP repositories and do not block web launch.
  • No production users or production customer dataset exists to copy; production AlloyDB starts empty.
  • Prisma 6.19/PostgreSQL; request/system work uses interactive DB transactions and database normalisation gates remain open.
  • The active GreyhoundIQ identity owns one billing-enabled free-trial project candidate, but no target Cloud Run, AlloyDB, load-balancer, storage, queue, monitoring or LiveKit resource has been provisioned or verified.
  • The repository's legacy workflow declares public single-region Cloud Run with default URLs; it is source evidence of an unsafe obsolete path, not live inventory for the new account.
  • The target API gateway, AlloyDB, application Memorystore, Pub/Sub, Cloud Storage and independent regional LiveKit cells are not deployed; no current backend exists from which CDN status can be inferred.
  • Thirteen racing-data pipelines are code-inventoried, but authoritative per-feed runtime health, ownership, licence, SLA, alert and runbook evidence is absent.
  • OpenAPI 3.0.3 covers 85 paths/106 operations; zero-error static Spectral evidence does not replace deployed negative tests.

Residency boundary

“Australia only” means Australian application compute and selected persistent application data. Google’s CDN/DNS/Monitoring and Secret Manager service semantics are global. Public CDN objects can be cached globally. WorkOS, Stripe and other authorised overseas providers require explicit cross-border and availability review; the self-hosted LiveKit media plane remains on Australian compute. Legal/DPA approval remains a launch gate for affected MVP journeys.

03
Critical journeys and workload classes

Protect outcomes, not every feature equally

Backpressure is intentional: lower-priority work is rejected, made asynchronous or disabled before it can consume the capacity required by identity, safety, payments and core racing workflows.

Priority 1–3

Critical

  • Session validation, recovery and account security
  • Core race/result/dog/track reads
  • Idempotent account and critical writes
  • Billing/webhook integrity and entitlements
  • Safety, moderation and audit evidence
Priority 4–6

Interactive

  • Feed and community interaction
  • Marketplace browse/enquiry/listing
  • Search and recommendation reads
  • Messaging presence/realtime
  • Uploads after signed acceptance
Priority 7–10

Sheddable / delayed

  • Reports and data exports
  • Analytics and bulk refresh
  • Recommendations and previews
  • AI/LLM generation
  • Email, enrichment and noncritical providers

Error budgets / 30 days

99.9% ≈ 43m 12s
99.95% ≈ 21m 36s
99.99% ≈ 4m 19s

Recommended recovery

Regional RTO ≤60 min and RPO ≤5 min. These are targets, not claims. Intra-region writer failure targets ≤5 min and zero acknowledged-write loss, subject to the failover test.

Error-budget policy

Page at 14.4× burn (5m + 1h) or 6× (30m + 6h). Freeze normal releases at 25% consumed in seven days, 50% consumed monthly, or any unresolved Sev-1.

Expected request profile

  • 6 dynamic + 8 static requests/user/min
  • 25% API cache hit; 95% immutable static hit
  • 32 KiB API and 64 KiB static response
  • 90:10 DB read/write; 4 DB operations/origin API request
  • 0.15 asynchronous jobs/origin request; 0.5 s/job

Excluded until separately modelled

Large uploads/downloads, video/media processing, report bytes/rows, full search indexes, AI provider tokens/cost, provider webhook bursts and cold first-load asset manifests. Each receives an independent quota and test before enablement.

06
Fifty-thousand-user calculations

The database equation closes before the autoscaler

Compute capacity stays symbolic until benchmarked. The 5/15/40 ms CPU cases are provisional sensitivities. Little’s Law with p95 is a conservative sizing proxy, not literal average concurrency.

API_RPS = peak_concurrent_users × dynamic_requests_per_user_per_minute ÷ 60 × burst_multiplier
ORIGIN_RPS = API_RPS × (1 − effective_cache_hit_ratio)
IN_FLIGHT ≈ RPS × response_time_seconds
REQUIRED_VCPU = origin_API_RPS × measured_CPU_seconds_per_request ÷ 0.60
REQUIRED_REPLICAS = ceil(required_vCPU ÷ allocatable_vCPU_per_replica) + failure/deploy/autoscale headroom
BANDWIDTH_bps = requests_per_second × response_bytes × 8
MONTHLY_TRANSFER = average_RPS × response_bytes × seconds/month
WORKER_CONCURRENCY = job_arrival_rate × job_duration ÷ 0.70
DB_OPS/s = origin_API_RPS × DB_ops/request
POOL_DEMAND ≈ DB_tx/s × tx_seconds ÷ 0.70
CONFIGURED_CONNECTIONS = all_app_replicas × pool_size_per_replica
At Scenario B expected normal load: 1,000 API RPS → 750 origin API RPS → about 3,000 DB operations/s. At a provisional 50 ms transaction and 70% pool target, connection demand is about 54. Current source can expose about 10 default application connections at max 10 instances. This is a launch-blocking hypothesis until the measured transaction and pooling model proves otherwise.

WebSocket stress

50k connections at 64 KiB = 3.05 GiB raw connection state; 3,333 heartbeat messages/s at 30 s; 1,667 reconnects/s if all return in 30 s. Provider quotas and a jittered reconnect test are mandatory.

Monthly sensitivity

*Monthly columns assume the displayed rate continues at a 20% duty factor and one 1 KiB structured origin log event/request. They are sensitivity estimates, not forecasts. CDN saves origin work, not delivered bytes.

Replica truth

Cloud Run abstracts availability zones; GreyhoundIQ cannot promise a chosen replica count per AZ. Each Australian region must have quota/caps capable of the selected N-1 load, and a controlled regional-loss test must prove the outcome.

08
Component-by-component architecture

Every component and racing feed has one owned contract

The registers state why each layer or feed exists, what reaches it, how overload or staleness is bounded, how a slow or incorrect response is detected, and what remains risky. “Managed,” “scheduled” and “publicly reachable” are never treated as proof of resilience, freshness or reuse rights.

Data-feed verdict: 13 code-backed pipelines across nine source families are inventoried. Their code paths and declared triggers are facts; production deployment, licences, named owners, refresh SLAs, degraded/down thresholds, alert delivery, runbooks and runtime evidence remain unknown. Current Admin source-health values are manually editable and therefore cannot be presented as authoritative live telemetry.

09
CDN, WAF, bot and DDoS

Reject hostile work at the cheapest layer

The origin is never sized to process arbitrary attack traffic. Edge controls absorb volumetric traffic, challenge or deny abusive HTTP traffic, and preserve a bounded admission budget for authenticated critical journeys.

DNS and domain

  • Cloud DNS anycast; registrar lock and phishing-resistant MFA
  • DNSSEC with registrar DS and rehearsed disable order
  • 300 s cutover TTL; normal 3600 s where safe
  • Certificate alerts at 30/14/7/1 days
  • Two-person reviewed zone/config rollback

CDN contract

  • One-year immutable hashed assets
  • Explicit public-media/public-read allowlist
  • Authenticated, tenant, admin, billing, messages and writes: private, no-store
  • Origin headers own TTL; no mixed FORCE_CACHE_ALL
  • Signed private access, purge/version and poisoning tests

Origin shield

  • Cloud Run ingress: internal and Cloud Load Balancing
  • Disable default URL on public web/API/realtime; retain only IAM-protected internal endpoints required by Google callers
  • No alternate A/CNAME or public object-store origin
  • Exact provider webhook paths only; signature and replay checks always
  • External direct-origin probe must fail
Cloud CDN is global. Public cacheable objects can be stored outside Australia and no city cache is guaranteed. Therefore private, authenticated, tenant-specific and legally restricted data never enters the shared CDN. Sydney/Melbourne storage is the authoritative object origin; legal approval owns the public-cache exception.

Cost-exhaustion ceiling

Cloud Run max instances are per revision and can be exceeded temporarily; they are not a hard financial ceiling. Protect cost with edge rejection, aggregate app admission, per-route/user/tenant/resource complexity quotas, separate worker caps, bounded queue depth, upload/report/AI budgets, logging sampling, 50/75/90/100% spend-velocity alerts and pre-tested optional-feature shutdown at 90%.

10
API gateway and load balancing

Three layers, three non-overlapping owners

GreyhoundIQ needs CDN + global external Application Load Balancer + ESPv2. It does not need managed API Gateway plus ESPv2, per-service internal load balancers or speculative service proxies.

Global edge / ALB

TLS, URL map and regional routing

Terminates TLS, preserves the trusted client-address chain, applies Armor/CDN, maps web/assets/API/webhook/admin paths and routes each request to the closest available functionally equivalent Sydney/Melbourne serverless NEG. Health-based failover requires Cloud Run service health/readiness, at least one minimum instance in each region, regional synthetics and a controlled failover test.

ESPv2 / Endpoints

Coarse API policy

Reject undeclared operations, validate supported token/API-key identity, enforce operation quotas and body/header/deadline budgets, version the API and emit per-operation telemetry. Generate Google extensions from the canonical OAS3 document; do not fork the contract.

Application + RLS

Authoritative access decision

Validate every schema and bound, enforce function/object/tenant authorisation, idempotency, CSRF/CORS, webhook signatures, business limits and PostgreSQL RLS. A gateway can deny; it can never grant an object action the application rejects.

Health and shutdown

  • /health: shallow process liveness; no provider calls
  • /ready: app startup and minimum critical dependency contract
  • At least one minimum instance remains available in each region
  • Dependency health appears on dashboards, not a cascading deep liveness probe
  • Stop admission, drain in-flight work, close pools, then terminate
  • No session affinity; externalise sessions and resumable state

Known platform limitation

Outlier detection alone is imperfect: it can converge slowly, and some requests can still reach an unhealthy region. No “healthy regional failover” claim passes until Cloud Run service health/readiness, regional warm floors, independent synthetics and controlled failure routing have been exercised against the exact configuration.

Cloud Run, with warm floors and hard downstream budgets

Managed containers best match the current Next.js monolith and team: faster operational maturity than GKE, fewer cold/timeout constraints than function-per-route, and less undifferentiated work than VMs.

Per-service contract

  • Same signed immutable digest in Sydney/Melbourne
  • 2 vCPU/4 GiB is a current source input, not approved sizing
  • CPU request/limit and memory limit set from profiles
  • Startup/readiness/liveness, CPU boost and image prewarming measured
  • Graceful drain and no new queue lease during termination
  • Worker and app have separate instance/concurrency caps

Scale policy

  • Warm floor covers measured startup plus sudden 3× interval
  • Concurrency set below p99/error/DB-pool knee
  • Regional cap ≥ full selected N-1 demand + 20% operational allowance
  • Combined caps fit DB connection and hourly cost budgets
  • Scale-down delayed until queue/SLO/DB recovery is stable
  • Quota and stockout alerts fire before configured maximum

12
Backend application architecture

Modular monolith, separately scaled workers

Traffic volume alone does not justify microservices. Keep relational transactions, authorisation and deployment simple; extract only a module with measured independent scale, security/data isolation or ownership need.

Synchronous application

  • Stateless request handling
  • WorkOS-backed sessions; no sticky sessions
  • OpenAPI versioning, bounded pagination/filters/bulk operations
  • Safe errors and cancellation/deadline propagation
  • Feature flags default to known-safe local values

Reliability primitives

  • Idempotency keys and duplicate ledger
  • Transactional outbox/inbox dedupe
  • Explicit deadlines and bounded retry budget
  • Circuit breakers, bulkheads and per-route concurrency
  • DLQ, poison quarantine and compensating actions

Security boundary

  • Deny-by-default server roles/permissions
  • Object/tenant authz before every read/write
  • RLS as defence in depth
  • PII/secret redaction allowlist
  • Admin reauth, two-person destructive approval and immutable audit

Emergency controls

Read-only mode, anonymous restriction, search/report/export/upload/AI disable, per-tenant isolation, queue pause, provider-circuit force-open, revision rollback, aggressive edge challenge and static maintenance response. Every switch has an owner, audit event, expiry, rollback and quarterly test.

13
Database and data architecture

Empty AlloyDB bootstrap; no customer-data cutover

Keep PostgreSQL and Prisma. GreyhoundIQ has no production users or customer dataset to copy: deploy the reviewed 107-model schema to an empty AlloyDB database with forward-only Prisma migrations, validate with synthetic staging fixtures, and rehydrate only approved racing-provider data through governed feed adapters. Compatibility and recovery still require isolated proof.

Current risk

  • One default Prisma connection/process versus concurrency 20
  • Request/system work takes interactive transactions
  • DB-backed rate limiter adds a write transaction and can fail open
  • Live DB CPU/connections/HA/backups/restore/roles remain unverified
  • Cloud Storage and application-realtime replacements remain unproven MVP blockers

Selected target

  • Empty AlloyDB PostgreSQL HA writer in Sydney
  • Matching Melbourne asynchronous secondary/read capacity
  • Forward-only Prisma schema bootstrap; synthetic staging identities and fixtures
  • Approved provider history rehydrated through validation, dedupe and lineage controls
  • Connection proxy/pooler only after Prisma/RLS/session-feature compatibility
  • Single writer with fenced emergency promotion; no active-active writes

Production starts empty; there is no source customer dataset or transfer workflow. Cross-region replication is asynchronous: abrupt-loss promotion has non-zero RPO and requires fencing plus reconciliation. Planned switchover may be zero-loss only while the primary and secondary are healthy, caught up and operated through a tested runbook.

Normalisation gate

The reviewed registry contains 29 not-verified database requirements: 4 M0, 14 M1, 7 M2 and 4 M3. Twenty-three block launch and 25 are mandatory before 50k. Priority defects include membership/owner authority, racing referential integrity, provider identity, nullable uniqueness, money types, billing idempotency and lineage, lifecycle constraints, typed roles/status, PII/audit attribution, bounded payloads, hot rows and Australian time correctness.

Empty bootstrap mandate

No production users or customer dataset exists to copy or catch up. Forward-only Prisma migrations create empty AlloyDB; protected staging uses synthetic identities/fixtures; approved racing-provider history returns only through governed validation, deduplication, provenance and reconciliation adapters.

MVP state replacements

Cloud Storage and application realtime must replace the legacy journeys before web MVP. Object replication is asynchronous: default target 99.9% within 1 hour/100% within 12 hours, or Turbo 100% within 15 minutes by ADR. Realtime uses the outbox, AU Pub/Sub, regional WebSocket gateways, separate application Redis and cursor replay. Required self-hosted LiveKit uses independent Sydney/Melbourne cells, application-persisted room home, regional HA Redis per cell, tested N+1 SFU capacity, TLS signalling, explicit UDP/ICE/TURN paths and visible call rejoin after regional loss.

14
Cache architecture

Disposable acceleration, never correctness

The database must survive zero dynamic-cache hit for critical traffic inside the selected admission budget. Memorystore Standard Tier is per-region and cross-zone only; it is not cross-region state. Cache improves margin, but a cache outage cannot be allowed to create an uncontrolled database outage.

Stampede

TTL jitter, request coalescing/single-flight, stale-while-revalidate, background refresh and one bounded fill per key.

Penetration/hot keys

Full flush

Reduce app/DB admission first, warm only the highest-value keys in a controlled ramp, serve accepted stale data and keep reports/search/AI disabled until DB reserve returns.

15
Queue and worker architecture

Durable intent before asynchronous convenience

Critical job intent is committed in the same PostgreSQL transaction as the business change, then relayed through Pub/Sub regional endpoints under a Sydney/Melbourne message-storage allowlist. That policy controls where Pub/Sub may persist messages; it does not copy every message to both regions. A topology ADR must select shared versus per-region topics/subscriptions and prove regional publish, backlog and replay behaviour. Sydney-only Cloud Tasks remains limited to reconstructable scheduling/throttling.

Queue invariants

  • At-least-once is assumed; every consumer deduplicates
  • Schema version, idempotency key and causal entity ID required
  • Retry deadline and max attempts per job class
  • Oldest age, arrival/completion, retries and DLQ alert
  • Unknown schema/poison message quarantines without blocking partition
  • Manual replay is scoped, audited and dry-run reviewed

Regional topology gate

Use regional endpoints. The ADR must name topic/subscription ownership, publish failover, persistence policy, duplicate semantics, ordering limits, backlog recovery and regional-loss user mode. Until that drill passes, the queue is not claimed as dual-region durable.

Worker overload rule

Worker concurrency = arrival_rate × average_duration ÷ 0.70, but the result is capped by the destination’s DB/API budget. Scenario B 10× produces an illustrative 1,125 jobs/s and ~804 worker concurrency at the placeholder mix—therefore optional jobs must backlog or disable rather than blindly create 804 workers.

16
Network and trust boundaries

Separate environments, private data plane, short-lived identity

Databases, caches, queues, internal dashboards and management interfaces never receive a public path. Control-plane systems are dependencies with explicit outage and compromise procedures. Dual-region resource labels never substitute for documented service semantics and a tested outage path.

Cloud hierarchy

  • Separate production and non-production projects
  • Dedicated security/log-archive project
  • Separate billing budgets and quota alerts
  • Org policies for regions, ingress, public access and service-account keys
  • Infrastructure state isolated, versioned and access audited

Data-plane network

  • Public edge only; app privately reaches DB/cache
  • Private services and regional endpoints where supported
  • Controlled egress through allowlists/proxy/NAT only where required
  • SSRF URL allowlists, DNS/IP revalidation and metadata protection
  • East-west service identity; mTLS only where it adds a real boundary

Administrative access

  • No shared bastion or permanent cloud keys
  • Workforce identity, phishing-resistant MFA and just-in-time role
  • Break-glass pair, sealed procedure and immediate rotation
  • Privileged action reason, session/audit record and dual approval
  • GitHub OIDC Workload Identity Federation for CI/CD

External identity; internal, deny-by-default authority

WorkOS can authenticate identities, but GreyhoundIQ owns every server-side role, function, object and tenant decision. The database RLS context is defence in depth, never a substitute for endpoint authorisation.

Session contract

Short access/session lifetime, rotating refresh where applicable, revocation and signing-key rotation tests, strict Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookies, CSRF on cookie mutations, clock-skew bound and replay-safe state/nonce. Exact lifetimes require risk and UX approval.

BOLA/BFLA gate

For every endpoint and sensitive server action, test unauthenticated, wrong user, wrong organisation/tenant, inactive/blocked actor, lower role, modified object ID, mass-assignment field and replay. Response uniformity must not disclose whether another object exists.

Scoped Staff Admin

Staff roles receive only named content, support, moderation, advertising, billing or routine operational permissions. They cannot self-promote, change release evidence, suppress audit, alter Founder ownership or operate infrastructure/recovery controls. Support access is case-bound, time-limited and reasoned.

Founder / Platform Owner control

Design Lab owner actions require a separate permission boundary, phishing-resistant MFA, recent reauthentication, JIT duration, reason, immutable audit and notification. Destructive, high-spend, bulk-export, production-write and recovery actions require two-person approval; controlled break-glass is separately exercised and rotated.

Secure delivery

Threat model, peer review, pinned dependencies, SAST, secret/dependency/IaC/container scan, SBOM, reproducible build, SLSA provenance, signed attestation, Binary Authorization and patch SLA.

API gate

Free pinned Spectral OWASP contract audit, authn/BOLA/BFLA/input/CORS/CSRF/replay/idempotency/429 tests, then bounded authorised Strix only after exact scope approval. Each is a separate gate.

AI guardrails

Strict tool allowlist, least-privilege identity, tenant-separated retrieval, prompt/indirect-injection filtering, untrusted-output validation, human approval for destructive actions, provider outage fallback and hard request/token/spend caps.

Observability and alerting

The Australia Observability Desk

Measure user outcomes and the four golden signals: latency, traffic, errors and saturation. Every page names an impact, automatic control, first human action, runbook and escalation route.

Current

Foundation only

Request header propagation, JSON warning/error logs, slow-query warning, health endpoints, route/load probe and five basic alert policies. End-to-end correlation, redaction, SLOs, alert delivery, region/edge/DB/queue/provider dashboards and drills are unverified.

Required

Telemetry contract

Validated request/trace ID, operation, region, revision, user-safe actor/tenant dimension, DB operation, event/job ID and deployment/config markers. Never log tokens, secrets, passwords, full payment data or sensitive payloads.

Resilience

Independent detection

Multi-vantage synthetic journeys and telemetry dead-man checks remain outside the application pipeline. Tamper-resistant regional security logs have separate access and retention.

Unified Admin desk

One operator surface joins SLOs, edge, API, compute, database, queue, feed, deployment and business-journey health through server-side least-privilege adapters. The browser never receives cloud credentials, billing export access, secret values or unrestricted logs.

Cost control

Show current and forecast spend by service/environment, budget consumption, cost per active user/1k API calls/report/upload, log/egress/NAT/cache-miss drivers and attack-driven scale. Alerts and optional-feature shutdown require a separate audited control path.

Data-feed diagnosis

Every feed shows last attempt/success/failure, source and destination watermark, lag, latency, counts, backlog, safe reason code, dependencies and affected journeys. Missing telemetry renders UNKNOWN—not healthy—and links to a tested retry/backfill/reconciliation runbook.

21
Deployment and rollback

Canary the immutable candidate; never reduce N-1 capacity

The current source smoke-tests a no-traffic candidate and then moves to 100%. The target adds progressive exposure, SLO gates, post-promotion validation and automatic rollback while the prior signed revision remains runnable.

Build and prove

Peer-reviewed IaC and code; pinned build; tests/security scans/SBOM; provenance and signature; exact config/migration/evidence digest.

Canary

Deploy no traffic, startup/readiness and synthetic checks, then 1% → 5% → 25% → 50% → 100% with observation windows appropriate to sharp and slow regressions.

Rollback

Stop on error/latency/burn/segment gate; route prior immutable revision; freeze deploys; validate data integrity and critical journeys; feature flag only when safer.

Compound deployment rule

If a zone/region is degraded, DB is failing over, monitoring is unavailable or a Sev-1 is active, freeze deployment and migration. A deployment may not consume the capacity needed to survive one Australian region/zone loss unless the incident commander explicitly accepts the risk and documents a rollback.

22
Backup and disaster recovery

A successful backup job is not a successful restore

Recovery is measured from incident declaration to validated user journeys and data integrity—not merely to a database endpoint becoming reachable. Emergency AlloyDB cross-region promotion is asynchronous and non-zero-RPO; planned zero-loss switchover is credible only while both regions are healthy and caught up.

Backup contract

  • Continuous PITR sufficient for target RPO
  • Daily retained copies and approved long-term schedule
  • Encrypted, isolated production access and cross-project AU recovery copy
  • Deletion protection/immutability and audited restore role
  • Backup age/completion and restore-test alerts

Restore cadence

  • Monthly representative row/table/PITR restore
  • Quarterly abrupt regional promotion, reconciliation and failback
  • Separate healthy planned-switchover exercise
  • Annual account-compromise reconstruction
  • Validate schema, RLS, counts, invariants, authz and app smoke
  • Record actual RTO/RPO and remediation

Current verdict

Production topology, backup retention, immutable isolation, restore time, point-in-time loss, writer fencing, Sydney failover and Melbourne promotion are unverified. Every recovery target is conditional, and zero-RPO is not claimed for emergency regional loss.

Target
Target ≤24h / ≤5m
EventSydney region lossDetails +
First containment
Read-only/critical mode; capture async lag/recovery point and fence former writer
Recovery method
Authorised emergency Melbourne promotion, app rollout, closest-available edge routing, reconciliation and later failback
Validation
Exactly one writer, measured non-zero RPO disclosed, auth/billing/core reads+writes/queues
Target
≤60m / approved measured RPO
Declare, contain and fence

IC confirms Sydney loss/data integrity, freezes writes/deploys, selects read-only/critical mode, captures asynchronous lag/recovery point and proves the former writer cannot accept writes.

Promote and validate

DBRE promotes Melbourne, updates secret/endpoint and application revisions in waves; verifies exactly one writer, RLS, migration, critical read/write and queues.

Restore, disclose and reconcile

Progressively restore edge traffic, disclose measured RPO, reconcile missing/duplicate work, create a new secondary and schedule controlled failback after stability.

23
Incident-response runbooks

An unfamiliar on-call engineer gets a safe first move

Each runbook records incident ID, UTC timeline, current revision/config digests, every containment mutation and evidence location. It never places secrets or private payloads in the incident record.

First 0–5 minutes

Confirm external impact; declare severity; freeze deploys/migrations/jobs; assign IC/ops/comms/scribe; open channel/timeline; classify edge/ingress/compute/DB/cache/queue/provider; check security indicators.

Minutes 5–15

Apply least destructive containment; tighten malicious traffic at edge or shed optional legitimate load; rollback suspected revision; protect DB; open slow-provider circuits; engage providers; publish first status.

Minutes 15–30

Verify containment externally and per region; decide normal/degraded/read-only/failover; validate data and queues; confirm monitoring/paging; set next decision point and update communications.

Critical quantitative gates

  • Scenario B normal: 30 min at 1,000 API / 750 origin API RPS; recommended SLO, CPU ≤60%, memory ≤70%, DB pool ≤70%.
  • 3× spike in 30 s: scale stabilises ≤120 s, critical transient errors ≤0.5%, no OOM/data loss, target recovery ≤5 min.
  • 10× in 2 min: optional work queues/sheds; critical reads ≥99.5%, writes ≥99.0% during event, DB ≤85%, cost ceiling holds.
  • Zero-cache, fleet restart + DB failover, provider slowdown, failed canary and one-region loss each preserve the documented mode without retry or reconnect collapse.
Latest local diagnostic, not staging capacity evidence: after the power-outage recovery rebound localhost to the existing loopback PostgreSQL volume, the same 25-request smoke improved from overall p95 44,033 ms and feed p95 44,172 ms to overall p95 3,733 ms and feed p95 1,998 ms, with 25/25 HTTP 200 and readiness healthy. Marketplace p95 remained 3,734 ms. No ARCH-701 credit is granted.

Three options, with attack and uncertainty priced in

Planning ranges are USD list-price estimates before GST, discounts, SaaS vendor fees, labour and incident cost. Confidence is low-to-medium until CPU/request, media egress, logs, DB size and duty cycle are measured in the Google Cloud Pricing Calculator.

Current anchors

Illustrative AlloyDB 4 vCPU/32 GiB ≈US$455/node-month; HA primary ≈US$909, matching one-node secondary ≈US$455. Storage, backup, network, support and insights extra.

Traffic anchors

5 TiB Oceania cached egress ≈US$563; 10 TiB ≈US$1,126. Endpoints at 50 average API RPS ≈129.6M calls/month and roughly US$383 after free tier.

Cost traps

Media egress, excessive logs/traces, NAT, cross-zone/region traffic, cache misses, report/export/AI abuse, queue retry storms, dual-revision scale, idle DR and oversized databases. The non-billable $300 Free Trial can fund only a time-bounded rehearsal of this full target; it is not a sustainable production budget. No paid upgrade, additional billing attachment or automatic payment is authorised.

ADRADR-001 · Cloud/regionDetails +
Decision / context
Selected target: Google Cloud; Sydney primary, Melbourne recovery; global defensive edge. Context: Australia-only product with existing GCP deployment material.
Options and criteria
GCP/AWS/Azure; AU services, current skills, managed resilience and team burden
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
Coherent managed stack and portability at logical layer; global edge/public caches and vendor processors remain residency exceptions
Reversal / reconsider when
High cloud reversal; reconsider for contractual sovereign-only processing, unavailable service or material cost evidence
ADRADR-002 · Region modelDetails +
Decision / context
Selected target: single-writer Sydney HA plus warm Melbourne application/data recovery—not active-active writes.
Options and criteria
Single region; backups only; warm DR; active-passive; active-active. Criteria: ≤60m/≤5m hypothesis, consistency and operability
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
Simplest design meeting recommended target; async lag and promotion/failback risk remain
Reversal / reconsider when
Medium-high reversal; reconsider if business approves weaker RTO or demands near-zero RPO with staffed operations
ADRADR-003 · ComputeDetails +
Decision / context
Selected target: managed Cloud Run containers in both AU regions with service health/readiness, ≥1 minimum instance/region, tested warm floors and hard workload admission.
Options and criteria
VMs, GKE, functions, Cloud Run, hybrid; scale speed, team load, connections, observability
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
Low host operations and fast regional scaling; soft maximums, cold starts and imperfect serverless-NEG outlier behaviour require controlled failover proof
Reversal / reconsider when
Medium reversal; reconsider for sustained high utilisation, unsupported persistent connections or controls needing GKE
ADRADR-004 · App boundaryDetails +
Decision / context
Selected target: stateless modular monolith; independently deployed async workers first.
Options and criteria
Monolith, modular monolith, services, microservices; scaling/isolation evidence and ownership
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
Fewer network/retry/data failure modes; web/API share fate until benchmark justifies a split
Reversal / reconsider when
Medium reversal; split only when measured resource isolation, security boundary or team ownership earns it
ADRADR-005 · CDNDetails +
Decision / context
Selected target: Cloud CDN allowlist for immutable assets, approved public media and reviewed anonymous reads only.
Options and criteria
No CDN, broad CDN, explicit allowlist; latency, attack resistance and privacy
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
Large origin reduction and AU edge latency; global cache is a residency/privacy constraint
Reversal / reconsider when
Low-medium reversal; remove a route from cache immediately if key/privacy/freshness proof fails
ADRADR-006 · Gateway/LBDetails +
Decision / context
Selected target: global external ALB + Armor/CDN + regional ESPv2; no managed API Gateway duplication.
Options and criteria
CDN only; ALB; API Gateway; ESPv2; layered. Criteria: TLS/routing, OAS policy, custom-domain maturity, overlap
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
Clear ownership and contract-derived API policy; extra gateway hop/configuration to operate
Reversal / reconsider when
Medium reversal; remove ESPv2 if no API-key/quota/schema value, or replace when a proven gateway requirement appears
ADRADR-007 · Primary databaseDetails +
Decision / context
Selected target: empty PostgreSQL/Prisma/RLS database on private AlloyDB; forward-only schema bootstrap, Sydney HA writer, Melbourne async secondary, synthetic staging fixtures and approved feed rehydration.
Options and criteria
Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, NoSQL/sharding; compatibility, pooling, failover and cost. No production customer-data migration option exists.
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
Retains relational integrity and code contract; RLS context, pool compatibility, fenced promotion and restore are launch blockers
Reversal / reconsider when
High reversal; shard only after vertical/index/cache/partition evidence; change database only if measured constraints justify redesign
ADRADR-008 · CacheDetails +
Decision / context
Selected target: browser/CDN first; independent Memorystore Standard per region only for proven hot data/coordination.
Options and criteria
No distributed cache, regional Standard Tier, query cache; hit benefit versus invalidation/DB failure
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
Cross-zone regional acceleration without treating cache as cross-region state; cache loss must never remove DB admission
Reversal / reconsider when
Low-medium reversal; add/resize when traceable hit ratio and cold-cache test justify it; never source of truth
ADRADR-009 · AsyncDetails +
Decision / context
Selected target: transactional outbox → Pub/Sub regional endpoints with Sydney/Melbourne persistence allowlist; shared versus per-region topic/subscription topology remains an explicit decision gate. Sydney Cloud Tasks is reconstructable work only.
Options and criteria
Shared topic, per-region topics, Tasks, external broker; durability, endpoint, ordering, failover and operations
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
Separates bursts and side effects; allowlist does not replicate each message, so failover/replay evidence remains blocking
Reversal / reconsider when
Medium reversal; choose topology only after regional publish/subscriber and backlog drills
ADRADR-010 · UploadsDetails +
Decision / context
Selected target: authenticated short-lived signed upload to private AU dual-region quarantine, asynchronous scan, then promote to separate serving origin; all MVP storage journeys replace the legacy path.
Options and criteria
App-proxied, direct-to-store, third-party media; abuse, size, malware, object RPO and cost
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
Removes large bodies from app and blocks execution on trusted origin; asynchronous object replication and scanner outage create exposure/backlog
Reversal / reconsider when
Medium reversal; default versus Turbo replication is selected in ADR-017; affected journey stays disabled until replacement tests pass
ADRADR-011 · IdentityDetails +
Decision / context
Selected target: retain WorkOS provisionally; server-side authz/RLS, passkey admin MFA, JIT and audited support access.
Options and criteria
Build auth, WorkOS, cloud identity; recovery, MFA, DPA and outage model
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
Avoids unsafe custom auth; US processing/outage and session-revocation semantics require explicit acceptance
Reversal / reconsider when
High reversal; change if DPA/residency, admin assurance or measured availability fails
ADRADR-012 · DRDetails +
Decision / context
Selected target: human-authorised emergency Melbourne promotion after recovery-point capture and writer fencing, progressive traffic shift, reconciliation and later failback; healthy planned switchover is separate.
Options and criteria
Backup restore, cold/warm/hot passive, active-active; RTO/RPO and human-error burden
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
Avoids multi-writer conflicts; abrupt loss is async/non-zero-RPO, while zero-loss planned switchover is possible only when healthy and caught up
Reversal / reconsider when
High reversal; automate only after repeated fencing, promotion, reconciliation and switchover exercises
ADRADR-013 · ObservabilityDetails +
Decision / context
Selected target: OpenTelemetry + Google Cloud metrics/traces, AU log buckets, immutable security audit sink and independent synthetics/paging.
Options and criteria
Cloud-native, SaaS, hybrid; residency, correlation, incident independence, cost
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
Full request-to-worker evidence and secondary detection; high-cardinality/log cost and global-metric metadata need governance
Reversal / reconsider when
Medium reversal; add vendor only for a measured capability gap and approved data path
ADRADR-014 · Design Lab control layerDetails +
Decision / context
Selected target: Design Lab is the authenticated simulation, managed-staging proof, training, observability and Founder release-authority layer; production remains read-only by default.
Options and criteria
Ordinary admin only, separate internal tool, Design Lab control plane; safety, parity and operator usability
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
One visible evidence/control model with strict local/staging/production proof labels; creates a privileged surface requiring independent IAM, JIT, audit and break-glass hardening
Reversal / reconsider when
Medium reversal; split the control plane if its blast radius, team ownership or compliance boundary cannot be isolated inside the web deployment
ADRADR-015 · Mobile clientsDetails +
Decision / context
Post-MVP decision: iOS/iPadOS and Android/tablet use independent repositories and release pipelines over the versioned backend contract; neither store app blocks web MVP production.
Options and criteria
Responsive web MVP, one later cross-platform app, two later native apps; UX, team, signing and release risk
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
No mobile build/signing/store secrets enter the web repo; backend compatibility is preserved without delaying web launch
Reversal / reconsider when
Medium-high reversal; native versus cross-platform is decided before mobile implementation, and store gates become blocking only for that release
ADRADR-016 · Racing feed operationsDetails +
Decision / context
Selected target: stable per-pipeline identities, authoritative server-side run telemetry, source-to-table lineage and fail-closed Admin/Design Lab health for all 13 feeds.
Options and criteria
One status per provider, manual admin flags, shared run ledger, per-pipeline telemetry; diagnosis, audit and operating cost
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
Pinpoints stale data and downstream impact without exposing credentials; adds run-ledger, threshold, alert and reconciliation ownership
Reversal / reconsider when
Low-medium reversal; merge feeds only when cadence, schema, failure and recovery boundaries are demonstrably identical
ADRADR-017 · Object replicationDetails +
Decision / context
Decision required before MVP storage enablement: choose Cloud Storage default asynchronous replication target (99.9% within 1h, 100% within 12h) or Turbo (100% within 15m).
Options and criteria
Default or Turbo; object RPO, recovery evidence, cost and workflow criticality
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
Makes object-loss exposure explicit; faster replication costs more and still requires restore/availability tests
Reversal / reconsider when
Low reversal by bucket/workload only after data-movement review; change when approved object RPO or cost changes
ADRADR-018 · Realtime/mediaDetails +
Decision / context
Selected MVP: regional Cloud Run WebSocket gateways with AlloyDB outbox, AU Pub/Sub, separate per-region application Memorystore and cursor replay; existing calls use independent self-hosted Sydney/Melbourne LiveKit cells with application-persisted room home, regional HA Redis per cell, tested N+1 SFU capacity, TLS signalling, UDP/ICE/TURN, native drain and explicit call rejoin after regional loss.
Options and criteria
Managed realtime, SSE, Cloud Run WebSockets, dedicated LiveKit VMs or GKE; latency, connections, room/participant capacity, networking, operations and cost
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
Removes legacy coupling, preserves DB authority and isolates media failure; adds application Redis, two isolated regional LiveKit Redis planes, cursor recovery, room routing and SFU/TURN operations
Reversal / reconsider when
Medium-high reversal; reconsider only from measured gateway or LiveKit capacity/operations evidence; native apps remain post-MVP
ADRADR-019 · Secret replicationDetails +
Decision / context
Decision required: user-managed Sydney/Melbourne Secret Manager replicas synchronously replicate versions, while Secret Manager remains global and write availability has separate semantics.
Options and criteria
Automatic or user-managed replication; cached versions; break-glass; read/write/rotation availability
Benefits / disadvantages / risk
Regional copies improve placement but do not prove control-plane independence or writable recovery
Reversal / reconsider when
Medium reversal; approve only after read/write/rotation outage drills and least-privilege review
Ledger boundary: the 70 items below are architecture work packages, not the full atomic Design Lab gate count. Database normalisation, operating-model, data-feed, screen, product and security registries remain separately derived and fail closed; their tasks must not be hidden or collapsed merely to keep this architecture summary concise. Native iOS/iPadOS and Android store delivery is post-MVP and does not block the web production gate.

28
Adversarial senior-engineer review

The design challenged before an outage does it for us

Each answer is resolved, accepted with owner, scheduled for validation or remains a launch blocker. None is hidden as a vague concern.

#QuestionDirect answer / status
1Most likely bottleneck?Database connection/transaction budget before raw Cloud Run CPU. Blocker · DBRE/App
2Assumption that most invalidates compute?Dynamic requests/user/min plus measured CPU and DB time per route. Benchmark P0.
3Where can retry storm occur?Client→gateway, app→provider, queue redelivery and fleet DB reconnect. One retry owner/deadline per edge; test compound failure.
4Every dependency slow?Bulkheads/deadlines shed optional features; critical admission remains. Slow-failure game day is blocked.
5Autoscaling cannot provision?Warm N-1 floor, priority admission, queues and Melbourne capacity; never remove DB/cost ceilings.
6One AZ fails at peak?Managed regional placement should absorb only after N-1 peak test; currently unproven.
7Zone fails during deployment?Deployment must abort while old+new remaining capacity holds N-1; gate currently unproven.
8Cache disappears instantly?Serve only bounded stale/single-flight traffic, shed cache-heavy routes and enforce DB admission.
9Can DB survive cache loss?Unknown until cold-cache Scenario B test; launch blocker.
10Can attacker bypass caching?Yes without key normalisation/cardinality quotas; edge and app limits plus test are required.
11Can attacker reach origin?Current public Cloud Run path appears possible; ingress/default-URL denial and external probe are launch blockers.
12Disproportionately expensive request?Search/export/report/upload/AI and high fan-out IDs; complexity, byte, row, time and concurrency budgets required.
13Authenticated attacker bypass per-IP?Yes; user/account/tenant/session/resource/complexity and global budgets remain authoritative.
14Can attacker cause uncontrolled cost?Current proof absent. Edge admission, per-revision max, worker caps, budget automation and log sampling must pass.
15Control likely to fail open?Current database-backed limiter behaviour unless fail-closed admission is implemented; security-critical routes must not rely on optional limiter.
16Control likely to block legitimate users?IP/geo WAF limits for CGNAT, mobile and overseas provider webhooks; preview/cohort synthetics and exact exceptions.
17Redundant but untested failover?Database and Melbourne regional promotion. Labels are not evidence.
18One-person knowledge dependency?DB promotion/failback and edge emergency changes until unfamiliar-on-call drill passes.
19Highest human-error recovery step?Promoting writer and later failback while preventing split brain/data divergence; dual approval and checklist.
20Unproven backup assumption?PITR isolation, retained logs, RLS/schema integrity and measured recovery point/time—all unproven.
21Identity provider unavailable?Existing proven sessions may continue; new login/recovery and risky admin fail closed; test exact token/revocation semantics.
22DNS/cert automation fails?External checks page before expiry/outage; reviewed rollback and emergency issuance. Drill outstanding.
23Monitoring unavailable during outage?Secondary synthetics/native metrics and audit sink; freeze changes. Correlated observability drill outstanding.
24Non-critical feature threatening critical path?Reports/exports/search/AI/realtime and media scanning via DB/provider/pool/log volume; isolate workers and kill switches.
25Where is tenant isolation enforced?Application object/function checks plus transaction-scoped PostgreSQL RLS; negative cross-tenant proof blocked.
26Sensitive data enters logs/caches where?Auth headers/cookies/request bodies/model context, cache-key mistakes and provider errors; allowlisted fields/no-store/redaction canaries.
27Unnecessarily complex for 50k?Active-active writes, GKE and microservices would be. Selected modular monolith + managed cells is intentionally simpler.
28Component removable without outcome loss?Managed API Gateway and service-specific internal load balancers; ESPv2+ALB already own those responsibilities.
29First principal-engineer challenge?No production workload or benchmark evidence, so all replica/cost figures remain sensitivity models.
30Most embarrassing post-outage discovery?A 'successful' backup that cannot restore within target or RLS context broken after failover. Both are launch blockers.

Final go / no-go checklist

NO-GO: target selected, production gates open

The current candidate is not production-ready. The checklist remains fail-closed until every conditional/fail item has exact passing evidence, an independent reviewer accepts it, and protected production approval binds the successful commit and immutable image digest.

# / requirementVerdictEvidence still required

4 · Lose one availability zone with capacityFailPeak N-1 zone-fault exercise and remaining-capacity record
5 · Deploy without dropping below safe capacityFailCanary/rollback plus zone-loss-during-deploy evidence
